spec.title: Answers seen by k6, by status
spec.description: One line per HTTP status. 202 = accepted, 413 = refused for size, 500 = server error, 0 = k6 got no answer (connection closed while sending). Each size is sent for about 10 s, so the picture is a staircase. Look for the size at which 202 turns into 413 or 500. Surprising: a 5xx other than 500, or 503 (that would be the breaker, not the size). k6 series are not marked stale after a run, so the last values can stay on screen for minutes.

spec.title: Answers counted by the API, by status
spec.description: The same answers as the API counts them (route unmatched = the body-parser answered before any route matched, which is how a 413 from the edge looks). Should agree with the k6 panel. Surprising: k6 sees 413 or status 0 that the API does not count (the connection was closed before the API could count it).

spec.title: Size of the cell that is running
spec.description: The level of the cell in bytes (body bytes, wire bytes for the wire levels, the big size for the mix cell), -1 between cells. Added by K12 (textfile ep_k12.prom, job node). Use it to read the other panels against the size.

spec.title: k6 latency p50 / p99 of the answer
spec.description: Time until the answer arrives, native histogram. For a big body this includes sending it. A fast 413 means the edge refused early; a slow 500 means the event went all the way to Kafka before failing.

spec.title: k6 requests that got no answer (status 0)
spec.description: Connection closed or timed out before an HTTP answer. Added by K12 (k6 counter resp_status0). Expected only for the biggest bodies if the server answers 413 and closes while k6 is still sending. Surprising: anything at small sizes.

spec.title: Records added to the topic vs acknowledged by the API
spec.description: Topic: sum over partitions of the log end offset, per second (kafka-exporter, topic k12-events). API: messages Kafka acknowledged. The two lines must be on top of each other. A 413 must add nothing to either. Surprising: the topic grows while the API says nothing was acknowledged (stored but reported as failed), or the API acknowledges and the topic does not grow (silent loss, the acks0 variant).

spec.title: Refused by the batcher (too large)
spec.description: ep_batcher_rejected_total with reason too_large: events above BATCH_MAX_BYTES that were refused before they were queued. This is the second layer. It should stay at 0 in the edge variant (the edge refuses first).

spec.title: Kafka send errors by type
spec.description: Failed batches by the client's error type. This is where the client limit and the broker limit show up, with their own names. Should be 0 when the edge or the batcher catches the event. Surprising: a type I did not predict, or 0 while the topic limit is lower than the event (then the failure was silent).

spec.title: Messages in failed batches
spec.description: Messages that were in a batch that failed or timed out. In the mix cell this is bigger than the number of oversized events, because the good neighbours in the batch fail with it.

spec.title: Batch size in bytes p50 / p99
spec.description: Bytes per flushed batch (all partitions together). The batcher cap is 900000 (1000000 in the client variant). One huge event is a batch of its own. Histogram buckets are coarse: a top bucket clamps the value.

spec.title: Poison in a batch: small and big events that failed
spec.description: Only in the mix cell (variant broker): small events (about 1,000 bytes) and oversized ones (400,000 bytes) that did not get 202. Added by K12 (k6 counters small_fail and big_fail). If the small failures are many times the big ones, one bad message takes its neighbours down.

spec.title: ingest-api process CPU
spec.description: CPU seconds per second of the API process (1 = one core). Parsing and validating a multi-megabyte body costs CPU even when the answer is 413 only after the body-parser read it. Pinned to 2 CPUs, so the ceiling is 2.

spec.title: ingest-api memory (RSS)
spec.description: Resident memory of the API. The API restarts for every cell, so the line is a sawtooth. A big body is held in memory (and copied for the Kafka message). Surprising: a jump that stays after a 413 cell.

spec.title: Host CPU busy by pinned group
spec.description: Busy share (1 - idle) of the CPUs of each pinned group. The load is small, so everything should be low. Brokers matter for the 880 KB events.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations
spec.description: Must be 0. Above 0 means k6 could not start requests on time (slow answers or no free VU); the cell did not send what it should.

spec.title: Generator CPU busy
spec.description: k6 CPUs (4,10). Keep under 70 %. Building a 5 MB body costs k6 CPU.

spec.title: Event-loop delay p99
spec.description: How long the API's event loop was blocked. Parsing a multi-megabyte JSON body blocks it. Surprising: long stalls on small cells.

spec.title: Under-replicated partitions
spec.description: Must be 0. The topic is deleted and recreated for each variant, so a short spike right after creating it is normal; a spike during a cell is not.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: what answer does each size get
2. The mechanism: who caught it, and did Kafka see it
3. Resources: what the big events cost
4. Validity: can I trust the run
EventPulse K12 - Message size and batch limits
